title: REST API Development Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Name a resource
examples.description: A resource is a thing an API exposes. /books/1 names one book, while /books names a collection.
examples.code:
GET /books/1 HTTP/1.1
Host: example.test

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{"id":1,"title":"Moon Trip"}

examples.title: Read without changing data
examples.description: GET asks to read a resource. Reading this collection does not add or remove books.
examples.code:
GET /books HTTP/1.1
Host: example.test

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

[{"id":1,"title":"Moon Trip"}]
examples.output: A list with one book is returned.

examples.title: Create a resource
examples.description: POST sends data for the collection to handle. A successful creation often returns 201 and a Location header.
examples.code:
POST /books HTTP/1.1
Host: example.test
Content-Type: application/json

{"title":"Sun Trip"}

HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Location: /books/2
Content-Type: application/json

{"id":2,"title":"Sun Trip"}
examples.output: Book 2 is created; its location is /books/2.

examples.title: Replace a known resource
examples.description: PUT supplies the desired representation at a known URL. This example replaces the book title and page count.
examples.code:
PUT /books/1 HTTP/1.1
Host: example.test
Content-Type: application/json

{"title":"Moon Trip","pages":30}

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{"id":1,"title":"Moon Trip","pages":30}

examples.title: Change part of a resource
examples.description: PATCH can send only changes. This example uses JSON Merge Patch to change the page count.
examples.code:
PATCH /books/1 HTTP/1.1
Host: example.test
Content-Type: application/merge-patch+json

{"pages":30}

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{"id":1,"title":"Moon Trip","pages":30}
examples.output: Only the page count is changed to 30.

examples.title: Remove a resource
examples.description: DELETE asks to remove the target resource. A 204 success response has no body.
examples.code:
DELETE /books/1 HTTP/1.1
Host: example.test

HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
examples.output: The book is removed; the response body is empty.

examples.title: Report an unknown item
examples.description: 404 means the requested resource was not found. A short error body can help a client explain the problem.
examples.code:
GET /books/99 HTTP/1.1
Host: example.test

HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"Book not found"}
examples.output: The API reports a missing book with status 404.

examples.title: Choose matching results
examples.description: A query string can describe a filter. The exact parameter names belong to the API design.
examples.code:
GET /books?colour=blue HTTP/1.1
Host: example.test

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

[{"id":1,"colour":"blue"}]
examples.output: Only matching blue books are returned.

examples.title: Read a small page of results
examples.description: Pagination divides a large collection into smaller pieces. This example returns a next link.
examples.code:
GET /books?limit=1 HTTP/1.1
Host: example.test

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{"items":[{"id":1}],"next":"/books?after=1&limit=1"}
examples.output: The client gets one item and a link for the next page.

examples.title: Describe the body format
examples.description: Content-Type says what format a body uses. Accept says which response formats the client can understand.
examples.code:
GET /books/1 HTTP/1.1
Host: example.test
Accept: application/json

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{"id":1}

examples.title: Repeat a request safely
examples.description: An idempotent operation has the same intended final effect when repeated. Setting pages to 30 twice leaves it at 30.
examples.output: The page count remains 30 after both PUT requests.

examples.title: Reuse an unchanged response
examples.description: An ETag labels a version. If-None-Match asks whether that version is still current. A 304 has no new body.
examples.code:
GET /books/1 HTTP/1.1
Host: example.test
If-None-Match: "book-v1"

HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
ETag: "book-v1"
examples.output: The client may reuse its cached book-v1 body.
